newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees Germany just above EMU debt threshold.
newsitem.headline: EU sees Germany just above EMU debt threshold.

text.p: The European Commission, in a review of Germany's economic convergence programme for monetary union, sees outstanding government debt hovering just above 60.0 percent of GDP in 1997, a source said on Thursday.
For 1998 and 1999, the EU executive sees the debt level ranging between 60.5 and 61.0 percent and declining by 0.5 percentage points in the year 2000.
In assessing Germany's programme the Commission also expressed doubts about a rapid reduction in unemployment.
"The Commission says that unemployment will be reduced less rapidly than expected," the source said.
There was no specific comment on Bonn's projected budget deficit of 2.9 percent of GDP in 1997.
Convergence programmes for both Germany and France will top the agenda of a meeting of EU finance ministers on Monday.
Regarding France, the Commission praised French efforts to reduce its budget deficit and the introduction of measures to keep expenditure under tight control.
But it doubted whether French economic growth projections of 2.5 percent in real GDP over the next few years could be attained.
"There is a risk that projected growth of 2.5 percent between 1998 and 2001 could not be attained," the source added.
France's convergence plan extends to the year 2001 while Germany's runs up to 2000.
The Commission, however, was optimistic that France could meet its projected budget deficit of 3.0 percent of GDP for 1997, the critical year for meeting the preconditions for monetary union.

"It's likely that the target will be achieved...given the economic growth forecasts and the discretionary measures announced," the source said. The Commission noted, however, there was a risk on both the revenue and expenditure side.
The Commission also said that beyond 1998 the French programme envisages a decline in the budget deficit to just above 1.0 percent of total output.
